newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-YANKEES TO BE HONORED WITH TICKER-TAPE PARADE.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-YANKEES TO BE HONORED WITH TICKER-TAPE PARADE.

text.p: Millions of revellers are expected to attend a Big Apple thank-you party for the World Series champion New York Yankees on Tuesday at a ticker-tape parade down New York City's Canyon of Heroes.
The Yankees captured their first World Series title in 18 years and the 23rd championship in their legendary history on Saturday night with a 3-2 victory over the Atlanta Braves.

A caravan of cars, fire trucks and other vehicles will carry Yankee players and officials through the streets of lower Broadway to City Hall. Mayor Rudy Giuliani will preside over the parade and ceremony.
Each player will receive a key to the city at the City Hall ceremony, which will also feature tributes to late Yankee slugger Mickey Mantle and sportscaster Mel Allen.
More than 2,000 police will be on duty, officials said.
The Yankees won the Series in stunning fashion, taking four in a row from Atlanta after losing the first two at home by a combined score of 16-1.
The win capped an emotional year for manager Joe Torre, who finally reached the World Series after 4,272 games as a player and manager.
Torre endured the death of his brother Rocco earlier this year and brother Frank spend most of the year in a hospital, awaiting a heart transplant he finally received on Friday.

The Series triumph was the 23rd for the Yankees since 1901, equalling the 23 Stanley Cups won by the National Hockey League's Montreal Canadiens, for bragging rights as North America's most successful professional sports team.
